steps.message:
You are computer-1, an autonomous agent that controls a desktop computer to
complete tasks. Each turn you observe the current screen via a screenshot and
respond with one action.

Task instructions:
GUI-only evaluation. Work in the Blender desktop using mouse and keyboard, observing screenshots. Do not open a terminal, Python Console, Scripting workspace, execute scripts or use command injection. You have no shell tool. Do not type code into Blender, a terminal, search box or editor to execute it. Use the task's native GUI operations to build from scratch, save the named .blend, and render/save outputs. You may type JSON into a plain text editor to save manifest.json; do not execute it. Use /app/materials and /app/material-previews (faithful PDF/table views of the supplied materials). Task reference solutions, grading scripts and prior runs are unavailable. Finish the work autonomously. Save progress frequently in /app/out. If the time limit arrives, preserve your actual partial output; do not claim missing deliverables exist.

You are working in a Blender 4.2 desktop session. `/app/materials` contains the
design pack for a weathered wooden shipping crate; `/app/out` is empty and is
where you deliver.

## What you are given

- `materials/drawings/crate_three_views.png` (and `.pdf`) — front / side / top
  views plus a corner-bracket detail, all dimensions in millimetres.
- `materials/spec/material_spec.pdf` — the material brief (weathered oak,
  rusted iron, worn stencil paint) and the render brief.
- `materials/photos/` — four reference photographs of the same crate.
- `materials/hdri/studio_soft.hdr` — CC0 studio environment.
- `materials/LICENSE.txt` — the licence for everything in the pack.

## What to build

Model the crate in Blender and render it. Use the GUI; the deliverable is a
scene a colleague can keep editing, not a screenshot.

1. Geometry, in metres:
   - five body panels `crate_front`, `crate_back`, `crate_left`, `crate_right`,
     `crate_bottom`, each exactly 20 mm thick, outer envelope 800 × 600 × 600 mm;
   - a lid `crate_lid`, hinged on the rear top edge, opening 0–95°, driven by a
     real pivot (an empty or the lid's own origin parented to one) — not a
     translate or a shape key;
   - eight corner brackets `bracket_01` … `bracket_08`, 60 × 60 × 2 mm, one per
     vertical corner, top and bottom, standing proud of the timber;
   - a stencil object `stencil_text` on the front face, white worn paint.
2. Edges are chamfered (bevel ≥ 2 mm). Panels and brackets are separate objects
   with real thickness; do not fake thickness with a texture.
3. Materials: weathered oak with 2K basecolor + roughness + normal maps (all
   packed into the .blend), rusted iron brackets with metallic 1.0, and stencil
   paint whose lettering is broken up by wear rather than a crisp new font.
4. Lights, cameras and the HDRI live in the file; every image is packed. The
   file must open and render after `/app/materials` is removed.

## What to deliver in /app/out

| File | Camera | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `crate.blend` | — | — |
| `render_front.png` | `cam_front`: 35 mm, 1.6 m from the crate centre, lens 0.9 m above the floor, front three-quarter | 1600 × 1200 |
| `render_back.png` | `cam_back`: same parameters, mirrored to the rear | 1600 × 1200 |
| `render_top.png` | `cam_top`: orthographic, covering 1.0 × 0.8 m | 1600 × 1280 |
| `render_macro.png` | `cam_macro`: 100 mm, 0.25 m from a top corner bracket | 1600 × 1200 |
| `manifest.json` | — | — |

Render with Cycles on CPU, 64 samples, denoising on, fixed seed. The four
cameras must be named exactly as above and kept in the file.

`manifest.json` follows the usual shape and must list every asset with a source
and a licence, including the HDRI:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "units": "meters",
  "blenderVersion": "4.2.3",
  "assets": [
    {"path": "hdri/studio_soft.hdr", "role": "hdri",
     "source": "self-authored", "license": "CC0-1.0", "url": ""}
  ],
  "renders": [
    {"file": "render_front.png", "camera": "cam_front",
     "resolution": [1600, 1200], "samples": 64}
  ]
}
```

## How it is checked

All of these must hold: the file reopens in Blender; all named objects exist;
outer size 800 × 600 × 600 mm ±5 mm; every panel 20 mm ±2 mm; the lid pivots at
the rear top edge and does not intersect the body at 0°, 45° and 95°; bevels
≥ 2 mm; three packed maps ≥ 2048 px wired to basecolor / roughness / normal;
wood roughness standard deviation ≥ 0.05; bracket metallic ≥ 0.9; the four
renders exist at the stated resolutions from the stated cameras; the manifest
covers the HDRI with a licence.

Two anti-cheat checks run against the delivered files. The scene is re-rendered
from `cam_front` and compared with your `render_front.png` (they must match), and
the lid is then rotated 60° and rendered again (the image must change).

Each delivered view/state is independently re-rendered from its specified
camera. It must match in every RGB channel (SSIM >= 0.90) and in image
structure (relative RGB gradient error after a 2-pixel Gaussian blur <= 0.60).
Agreement on a large uniform background alone is insufficient. Compositing
or a video sequence cannot substitute for the delivered 3D scene.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task.


You interact with the computer through a private runtime. On every turn you
will see a fresh screenshot of the current desktop. The display is
1920x1080 pixels. All click/move/scroll/drag
coordinates you produce MUST be in raw desktop pixels (no normalization).

Initial screen state:
see attached screenshot.

Response format
===============

Respond with EXACTLY one JSON object and nothing else (no surrounding prose,
no Markdown fences). The object must validate against this shape:

{
  "analysis": "<short notes about the screen / progress>",
  "plan": "<your plan for the next few steps>",
  "action": {
    "type": "<one of: click, double_click, triple_click, right_click, mouse_down, mouse_up, mouse_move, type, keypress, hold_key, scroll, drag, zoom, navigate, wait, done, answer>",
    "x": <int, optional>,
    "y": <int, optional>,
    "end_x": <int, optional, only for drag>,
    "end_y": <int, optional, only for drag>,
    "text": <string, optional, used by type and answer>,
    "keys": <list of strings, optional, used by keypress and hold_key>,
    "url": <string, optional, used by navigate>,
    "scroll_x": <int, optional, used by scroll>,
    "scroll_y": <int, optional, used by scroll>,
    "button": <"left"|"middle"|"right", optional, used by click>,
    "modifier": <"shift"|"ctrl"|"alt"|"super", optional, held during click/double_click/triple_click/right_click/scroll>,
    "duration": <number of seconds, optional, used by hold_key>,
    "zoom_region": <[x0, y0, x1, y1] in desktop pixels, optional, used by zoom>,
    "result": <string, optional, the final answer for done/answer>
  }
}

Rules
=====

- Output exactly ONE action per turn. Do not batch.
- For "click", "double_click", "triple_click", "right_click", "mouse_move",
  "mouse_down", "mouse_up", "scroll", "drag": provide raw desktop pixel
  coordinates in "x"/"y" (and "end_x"/"end_y" for drag).
- For "type": provide the literal text in "text". The text is sent to the
  currently focused field.
- For "keypress": provide a list of key names in "keys" (e.g. ["ctrl", "l"]).
- For "hold_key": provide "keys" plus "duration" in seconds. The keys are
  pressed, held for "duration" (default 1s), then released.
- For "scroll": provide "scroll_y" in pixels (positive=down, negative=up) and
  optionally "scroll_x" (positive=right, negative=left). Pass "modifier" to
  hold a key (e.g. "ctrl" for zoom-scroll).
- For click variants and scroll, set "modifier" to one of "shift"/"ctrl"/
  "alt"/"super" to hold that key for the duration of the action.
- For "zoom": provide "zoom_region" as [x0, y0, x1, y1] in desktop pixels.
  The NEXT screenshot is cropped (no resize) to that region, then auto-resets.
  Use this to inspect a small UI area at native pixel density.
- For "navigate": provide the destination URL in "url".
- For "wait": no fields are required; the runtime will pause briefly.
- When you have completed the task, emit a "done" or "answer" action with the
  final answer in "result". The harness writes "result" to
  /logs/agent/final_answer.txt for the verifier.

Output the JSON object now.
